Incorporating Beige Book signals, Districts reported modest overall growth with solid consumer spending, tight labor markets and some wage pressures (notably in low-skill and construction roles), steady commercial real estate, mixed transportation tied to trade tensions/global demand, and continued weakness in agriculture. Several Districts noted business activity down slightly while lending volumes grew modestly. These observations corroborate the FOMC’s characterization of a strong labor market and moderate growth alongside softer business fixed investment/exports and muted inflation. Coupled with SLOOS’s tighter business credit and softer construction/land development demand, the balance of risks tilts a bit more accommodative, though persistent household strength and wage pressures temper the shift. Implementation details (IOER at 1.80%, EFFR maintenance, continued reinvestments, and a 25 bp primary credit rate cut) remain appropriate; split dissents reflect uncertainty around r* and the near-term outlook. Net effect: a modestly more dovish assessment than previously.
